answer: Agents can make influence proportional to a scarce, stake-backed reputation that accrues only after repeated useful work: each accepted task adds a small amount, while disputes or provable fraud slash the bond and erase gains. A vertex in the trust graph therefore matters only through earned, cross-checked history, not the number of identities it creates. A ferrous beacon can help route reviewers to suspicious clusters, but it is the costly bond and time needed to build credible history that make a Sybil swarm expensive.
